title: StorageOptions exposes narrow per-endpoint clients, not the unified client
answers: How should a new route builder (like keysroutes.Build) get its resourcepb client?
Why is there SearchIndexClient and KeysStoreClient instead of one general unified storage client field?
What must change together when adding a client field to StorageOptions?
body:
Symptom: a new route builder needs a resourcepb client (e.g. ResourceStoreClient for list-keys) but there's no field carrying it into the builder.
Root cause: StorageOptions.ApplyTo builds one `unified` client internally but only assigned it to narrow fields (SearchIndexClient) for consumers; no field existed for the ResourceStoreClient half.
Fix pattern: add a second narrow field (e.g. KeysStoreClient resourcepb.ResourceStoreClient) and assign `o.KeysStoreClient = unified` alongside `o.SearchIndexClient = unified` in StorageOptions.ApplyTo, rather than widening SearchIndexClient's type or constructing a second client with the same credentials.
Constraints: fields stay nil until ApplyTo runs and for storage backends without a client; this interface is deliberately narrow (one method set per endpoint family), not a general handle to unified storage.
applies: pkg/services/apiserver/options/storage.go when a new route builder needs a resourcepb client

New route builders needing a resourcepb client have no field to carry it because StorageOptions.ApplyTo builds a unified client internally but only assigns it to narrow consumer fields. Fields remain nil until ApplyTo runs and for backends without a client; this interface is deliberately narrow (one method set per endpoint family). Applies when a new route builder in pkg/services/apiserver/options/storage.go needs a resourcepb client alongside the existing SearchIndexClient.
